records.issue_text: packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:254 — When externalCalendarId is absent, the fallback searches for a destination matching that absent ID, preventing updates and deletes from targeting existing events on configured non-primary calendars.
records.rationale: The diff changes the fallback in updateEvent (and deleteEvent) from `event.destinationCalendar?.externalId` to `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId`. When externalCalendarId is absent/falsy (the very case the fallback exists for), no destination calendar can have an externalId equal to the absent value, so find() always returns undefined and the fallback yields undefined instead of a valid calendar ID — breaking updates/deletes that previously targeted the destination calendar. This is a verifiable defect introduced by this diff.

records.issue_text: packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts:1079 — When the organizer has no destination calendar, evt.destinationCalendar is null, so optional chaining silently discards collected teammates’ destinations instead of appending them to an initialized array.
records.rationale: The diff sets evt.destinationCalendar to null when neither eventType.destinationCalendar nor organizerUser.destinationCalendar exists, then later does `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)` — optional chaining on null silently drops collected teammates' destination calendars for collective team events, so their calendars are skipped. The mechanism is visible in the diff lines at handleNewBooking.ts (destinationCalendar ternary ending in `: null` and the `?.push(...)` call).
